<a id="aunt_clara"></a>
## Light-Jazz Sitcom Theme: `aunt_clara.yml`

A twinkling light-jazz sitcom theme of the sixties in the manner of the Bewitched theme (Howard
Greenfield and Jack Keller), with a tune of its own. A swinging ride, a walking bass and plucked
strings; a vibraphone with a skipping tune on I vi ii V, a celesta sparkling after each phrase; a
bridge through four dominant chords; choruses for a muted trumpet and a flute.

<a id="come_on_down"></a>
## Game-Show Theme: `come_on_down.yml`

A bright seventies game-show theme in the manner of The Price Is Right theme (Edd Kalehoff), with a
tune of its own. A brass section and a synthesizer in unison on a leaping tune, a clavinet chopping
sixteenths, funky bass octaves and a busy drum kit with a tambourine; a bridge, a flute chorus and a
drum break.

<a id="eats_cats"></a>
## Slap-Bass Sitcom Theme: `eats_cats.yml`

A bouncing mid-eighties sitcom instrumental in the manner of the ALF theme (Alf Clausen), with a
tune of its own. A slap bass alone, then a drum machine and an electric piano; a syncopated synth
brass tune over I, vi and the flat seventh; a second strain and a sax chorus.

<a id="forgot_your_name"></a>
## Sitcom Theme: `forgot_your_name.yml`

A warm piano sitcom theme in the manner of Cheers (Gary Portnoy), with a melody of its own. A piano
alone under a quiet verse on I and V, then the band, strings and a choir for a chorus that opens out
on I bVII IV V; a bridge, and the piano alone to end.

<a id="laboratory_mice"></a>
## Orchestral Cartoon Theme: `laboratory_mice.yml`

A mock-sinister orchestral cartoon theme of the nineties in the manner of the theme of Pinky and the
Brain (Richard Stone), with a tune of its own. A tuba and plucked strings in a swung two-beat; a
bassoon creeping through a minor tune on i, V7 and iv; a grand refrain in the relative major for
choir and brass; a sneaking stretch for plucked strings and a whistle.

<a id="meeting_the_eye"></a>
## Hard-Rock Cartoon Theme: `meeting_the_eye.yml`

A one-minute hard-rock cartoon theme of the mid eighties in the manner of the theme of The
Transformers (Ford Kinder and Anne Bryant), with a tune of its own. The band plays the slogan's
rhythm alone, then the voices shout it; a chorus on i VII i V and VI VII i that a robot voice
answers; one low verse; a drum break with the robot alone; the chorus and the slogan again.

<a id="mysterious_spooky"></a>
## Creepy Harpsichord Theme: `mysterious_spooky.yml`

A creepy, kooky harpsichord theme in the manner of The Addams Family (Vic Mizzy), with a tune of its
own. A short, low harpsichord figure answered by two snaps, played on one chord and then a step
higher; a bouncing tune over a tuba, with a dominant chord on II; a reed organ takes the tune in the
middle.

## Wistful Guitar Theme: `not_painless.yml`

and strums a nylon guitar's chords, which a Progression takes round the circle of fifths in minor.

<a id="sax_reindeer"></a>
## Novelty Saxophone Romp: `sax_reindeer.yml`

A breakneck novelty saxophone romp in the manner of Yakety Sax (Boots Randolph), with runs of its
own. A tenor sax running in sixteenths over a country two-beat, bass on one and three and the piano
and guitar on the offbeats, a train beat on the snare; a second part that wails on long notes over
IV, I and a dominant II; the last time a step higher.

<a id="spy_hunting"></a>
## Spy Theme: `spy_hunting.yml`

A late fifties spy-jazz theme in the manner of Peter Gunn (Henry Mancini), with a riff and a tune of
its own. One bar of low eighths on a twangy guitar, a piano and a bass, on one chord, that never
stops; brass chords that swell over it; a head in long blue notes and a wailing tenor sax solo;
once, the riff moves to iv and back.

<a id="three_hour_tour"></a>
## Sea-Shanty Sitcom Theme: `three_hour_tour.yml`

A sea-shanty sitcom theme of the sixties in the manner of The Ballad of Gilligan's Isle (Sherwood
Schwartz and George Wyle), with a tune of its own. A shanty in minor on i and VII, strummed by a
Guitarify on an acoustic guitar with an accordion and men's voices; each verse a half step higher,
from D minor to F minor.

<a id="tropical_51"></a>
## Big-Band Police Theme: `tropical_51.yml`

A big-band police-show theme in the manner of Hawaii Five-0 (Morton Stevens), with a fanfare of its
own. Tom-toms and timpani open, then a trumpet fanfare in bold leaps over a driving bass, tambourine
and brass on the offbeats, the chords falling i VII VI to a major V; trombones answer; and the whole
thing rises a step, twice.

<a id="uk_butler"></a>
## Ragtime Sitcom Theme: `uk_butler.yml`

A saloon-piano ragtime sitcom theme in the manner of the Mr. Belvedere theme (Judy Hart-Angelo and
Gary Portnoy, as Leon Redbone sang it), with a tune of its own. A honky-tonk piano opens alone with
a rag figure over a low note and a chord by turns; a lazy tune over ragtime chords, the piano
filling each gap; the piano takes a chorus in octaves; a scatted tag on a muted trumpet.

<a id="uphill_cops"></a>
## Voice-Led Piano Theme: `uphill_cops.yml`

A gentle piano theme in the manner of Hill Street Blues (Mike Post), its chords voice-led, with a
melody of its own. An electric piano rolls each chord gently, I and IV in turn, under a plain piano
tune of long notes; a soft rhythm section, a clean guitar that fills the gaps and strings join; a
second strain climbs through IV V iii vi.
